Christ is signified in the precious stone, the apostles in the pearls; in the white fine linen, the justifications of the saints; in the purple, martyrdom; in the silk, virginity; in the red scarlet, charity; in the incorruptible thyine wood, unfailing constancy; in the ivory, the beauty of virtues; in the brass, fortitude and longanimity; in the iron, the keenness of loftiness; in the marble, unconquered humility. These the reprobate pretend to have, and they grieve when what is understood in them fails. In the gold we take worldly wisdom; in the silver, eloquence; in the precious stone and pearls, false prophets and heresiarchs; in the fine linen, feigned justice; in the purple, the martyrs of heretics; in the silk, integrity of the flesh as a covering for a corrupt mind; in the scarlet, cruelty cloaked with a pretence of charity; in the thyine wood, obstinacy of mind feigning constancy; in the ivory, feigned beauty of virtues. By the ointment, the incarnate divinity, which the harshness of false Christians imitates under a false gentleness.
